elements.quote: Purpose The objective of this systematic review is to compare the safety and efficacy of surgical fixation of rib fractures against non-surgical interventions for the treatment of flail chest in the adult population.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly identifies the work as a systematic review.

elements.quote: Purpose The objective of this systematic review is to compare the safety and efficacy of surgical fixation of rib fractures against non-surgical interventions for the treatment of flail chest in the adult population.
elements.reason: The abstract states the main objective/review question.

elements.quote: Relevant randomised controlled trials were selected, their risk of bias assessed, and the data then extracted and analysed.
elements.reason: The abstract indicates that relevant randomized controlled trials were selected, but it does not provide explicit main inclusion and exclusion criteria.

elements.quote: Methods A search was performed on the 22nd of July 2020 to identify articles comparing surgical fixation versus clinical management for flail chest in adults, with a description of the outcome parameters (resource utility, mortality, adverse effects of the intervention and adverse progression in pulmonary status).
elements.reason: The abstract gives the search date but does not specify the information sources/databases searched.

elements.quote: Relevant randomised controlled trials were selected, their risk of bias assessed, and the data then extracted and analysed.
elements.reason: The abstract states that risk of bias was assessed, but it does not specify the methods/tool used.

elements.quote: Relevant randomised controlled trials were selected, their risk of bias assessed, and the data then extracted and analysed. Results 157 patients were included from four studies in the analyses, with 79 and 78 patients in the surgical and non-surgical groups, respectively. The pooled effects of all outcomes tended towards favouring surgical intervention.
elements.reason: The abstract indicates data extraction and that pooled effects were calculated, but it does not describe the full methods used for presenting and synthesizing results.

elements.quote: Results 157 patients were included from four studies in the analyses, with 79 and 78 patients in the surgical and non-surgical groups, respectively.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the total number of included studies and participants and provides group sizes.

elements.quote: The pooled effects of all outcomes tended towards favouring surgical intervention. Surgical intervention was associated with lower rates of pneumonia ( I 2 = 46%, Tau 2 = 0.16, p = 0.16), significantly lower rates of tracheostomy ( I 2 = 76%, Tau 2 = 0.67, p = 0.02), and a significantly lower duration of mechanical ventilation ( I 2 = 88%, Tau 2 = 33.7, p < 0.01) in comparison to the non-surgical management methods.
elements.reason: The abstract presents results for main outcomes (pneumonia, tracheostomy, duration of mechanical ventilation) with comparative findings.
Although the abstract mentions pooled effects, it does not report a summary estimate with a confidence interval or credible interval for the meta-analysis.

elements.quote: The pooled effects of all outcomes tended towards favouring surgical intervention. Surgical intervention was associated with lower rates of pneumonia ... significantly lower rates of tracheostomy ... and a significantly lower duration of mechanical ventilation ... in comparison to the non-surgical management methods.
elements.reason: The abstract indicates direction of effect (favoring surgical intervention) and which group has better outcomes.

elements.quote: There is a need for further well-designed studies with sufficient sample sizes to confirm the results of this study and also detect other possible effects of surgical intervention in the treatment of traumatic flail chest in adults.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a form of limitation (need for further well-designed studies/sufficient sample sizes), but it does not explicitly summarize limitations of the included evidence such as risk of bias, inconsistency, or imprecision.

elements.quote: Conclusion Our results suggest that surgical intervention reduces the need for tracheostomy, reduces the time spent in the intensive care unit following a traumatic flail chest injury and could reduce the risk of acquiring pneumonia after such an event.
elements.reason: The abstract gives a general interpretation and implications of the findings.
The abstract does not report the primary source of funding.
The abstract does not provide a register name and registration number.

elements.quote: Even so, more well-designed multi-centred RCTs are needed to produce strong evidence that could influence clinical practice.
elements.reason: Some uncertainty/knowledge gaps are implied by the need for stronger evidence from future multi-centre RCTs, but the broader current state of knowledge and important uncertainties are not described in detail.

elements.quote: The results of this systematic review are by and large consistent with the results seen in the previous retrospective studies and meta-analyses [22-24]. However, previous studies [23-25] only included three of the RCTs and reported on 61 patients whilst this study includes 4 RCTs with 157 patients in total. Hence, our study is more conclusive than these previous studies due to the larger number of patients involved in surgical fixation.
elements.reason: The evidence gives a rationale related to why a review is needed to provide more conclusive evidence, but it does not clearly and explicitly explain the overall importance and need for conducting the review in the context of existing knowledge.

elements.quote: The results of this systematic review are by and large consistent with the results seen in the previous retrospective studies and meta-analyses [22-24]. elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly discusses prior reviews/meta-analyses and explains how the current work differs (more RCTs/patients), thereby explaining the need for the current review in light of existing evidence.
No proposed mechanism of action of surgical fixation (as a treatment effect pathway) is described in the retrieved evidence.
No logic model or hypothesised relationships between intervention components and outcomes are provided in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Purpose The objective of this systematic review is to compare the safety and efficacy of surgical fixation of rib fractures against non-surgical interventions for the treatment of flail chest in the adult population.

elements.quote: Purpose The objective of this systematic review is to compare the safety and efficacy of surgical fixation of rib fractures against non-surgical interventions for the treatment of flail chest in the adult population.

elements.quote: Studies were only included if they meet the following inclusion criteria: (1) prospective RCTs, (2) comparing surgical treatment against non-surgical, clinical management of flail chest injury. ... elements.quote: Although surgical stabilisation is indicated by our systematic review of this small number of RCTs, when surgery for flail chest is indicated or the timing of surgery remains unclear. For example, in one study, patients were only enrolled if they were dependent on a ventilator with no prospect of successful weaning within the next 48 h [12]. Other studies did not mention the reasons why patients were included in their study or what criteria they used to judge when surgical fixation over non-surgical management was best. Likewise, the timing of surgical stabilisation in one study occurred 5 days after the initial injury [11]; however, other studies did not mention the timing of surgical intervention from initial injury. These two important parameters could have added variability to the outcomes of surgical management.
